hints.title: Key Insight and Observation
hints.text: Two intervals [s1, e1] and [s2, e2] intersect if and only if neither interval ends strictly before the other begins.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy and State
hints.text: Sort start times and end times into separate ascending arrays.

hints.title: Optimal Boundary and Processing
hints.text: For each interval, count how many intervals finish strictly before its start time using search comparisons.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import bisect

def countIntersectingIntervalPairs(intervals: list[list[int]]) -> int:
    n = len(intervals)
    if n <= 1:
        return 0

    total_pairs = n * (n - 1) // 2
    # Disjoint pairs: interval A ends strictly before interval B starts (A.end < B.start)
    ends = sorted(iv[1] for iv in intervals)

    disjoint = 0
    for s, e in intervals:
        # number of intervals ending strictly before s
        disjoint += bisect.bisect_left(ends, s)

    return total_pairs - disjoint
```

complexity.notes: Sorting endpoints followed by binary search counting of disjoint pairs.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Direct nested comparison of all interval pairs requires quadratic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Endpoint arrays store n numbers each.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Counts disjoint intervals via sorted ends to deduce intersections.
